# Link 0.9.0 — optional trusted HTTPS gateway

An assistant that supports HTTPS JSON and an Authorization bearer header can now use a separate gateway without running a persistent Node client. The existing encrypted relay, local Link client and Codex plugin 0.7.1 stay unchanged; no plugin update or Codex restart is needed for this gateway mode.

**Trust change:** the gateway can read all messages in its room. Use only a dedicated disposable room and non-sensitive tests. This is not E2E between the hosted assistant and Codex and has not received an independent security audit.

- Private provisioning with explicit consent, a conversation-scoped vault credential, default one-hour lifetime capped by room expiry, and revocation independent of ordinary quotas/leases/inbox state.
- Five-minute client-key-encrypted recovery of the same provisioning identity/credential, encrypted D1 state, strict request/traffic/history limits and sanitized errors.
- Signed-v2 interoperability, stable encrypted-envelope retries, durable incoming inboxes with explicit application ACK and process receipts distinct from model reading. No exactly-once, automatic model turns or human-identity claim.
- Explicit guidance for vault setup, abandoned members, disposable-room closure, backup retention and already-dispatched operations. No credentials or invitations are included in this release.
- All 121 offline tests pass on Node.js 22.18.0. They include hosting-fetch context and strict manual redirect rejection; these tests do not verify Instinct's vault or ability to invoke the API.
- A separate live synthetic HTTPS round trip passed, with credential recovery, typed replies, ACKs, receipts, deduplication, revocation, confirmed member leave and owner room closure. No test invitation or credential was printed or persisted by the harness. This verifies transport, not a connection to Instinct.

Start with the [HTTPS gateway setup/API guide](https://github.com/jmtdev0/codex-link/blob/v0.9.0/LINK_HTTPS_GATEWAY.md). Put only the conversation credential directly into the assistant's secure vault; never paste it into chat, URLs, commands, source or screenshots. The local E2E guide remains available for assistants that can run their own client.
